title: Trip Stories
how_it_works_companion: How It Works chapter 10, section HOW MEMBERS RECORD A TRIP

sections.business_context:
After a trip, a member can write an account of it - answering questions the club sets about the car, the
drive and the company - and keep it with photographs from the trip. It belongs to the member. The
club stores it and does not read it as operational data.
Pairs with How It Works chapter 10, section HOW MEMBERS RECORD A TRIP.
sections.schema_overview:
TABLES USED BY THIS GUIDE

Table                             Role in this guide

MEMBER_TRIP_STORY                 One story per trip: its title, introduction, and cover photograph.

MEMBER_TRIP_STORY_PROMPT The questions, held as data so the club can change them.

                                  One answer per prompt, keeping the member’s words separately from any
MEMBER_TRIP_STORY_ANSWER
                                  assisted version.

VEHICLE_TRIP                      The trip the story is about.

DOCUMENT, DOCUMENT_LINK           Photographs, linked to the trip.
sections.implementation_workflow:
1. Offer the story once the trip is closed. A trip still open has no ending to write about.
    2. Read the prompts from MEMBER_TRIP_STORY_PROMPT in sort_order, active only. Never
       hard-code the questions: the club will change them, and the ones that produce good writing
       are not known yet.
    3. Save answers as the member types rather than on submit, stamping last_saved_at. A member
       writing about a weekend should not lose it to a closed tab.
    4. Store photographs as documents linked to the trip through DOCUMENT_LINK. The cover
       photograph is a pointer on the story, not a separate upload.
    5. Write answer_text only. assisted_text and assisted_at are reserved for a future integration;
       nothing in this build writes them.
sections.rules_and_constraints:
1. One story per trip, enforced by a unique constraint on vehicle_trip_id.
    2. The member who took the trip writes and reads their own story; that needs no permission.
       Staff access to somebody else’s story requires manage_member_story, which is held by
       managers and above, and exists for support and for removing content where necessary rather
       than for browsing.
    3. A prompt that is deactivated stops being offered but its existing answers remain and still
       display.
    4. assisted_text never replaces answer_text. The member’s own words are kept whatever else is
       generated.

    5. uses_assisted decides which version is displayed and defaults to the member’s own.
sections.integration_and_edge_cases:
1. A trip cancelled or reversed after a story is written. The story stays with the trip record; do
       not delete somebody’s writing because an operational record changed.
    2. A shared membership. The story belongs to the member who took the trip, not to everybody
       on the package.
    3. A member who answers nothing. An empty story is not created. A story exists once there is
       something in it.
    4. A prompt reworded after answers exist. The answers stay attached to the prompt they were
       written for; the reworded question applies to stories written afterwards.
sections.automations_and_notifications:
AUTOMATIONS IN THIS GUIDE

Trigger                         Outcome

Trip closed                     Member invited to write about the trip.

Story left unfinished           Nothing. The club does not chase a member for a story.
sections.developer_notes:
1. Prompts are data, not columns. Ten fixed columns would have been simpler to write and
       would need a migration every time the club changed a question.
    2. The assisted fields exist now and are written later. Adding them at the start costs nothing
       and means the integration, when it comes, does not touch the shape of the data.
    3. Photographs link to the trip rather than to the story, so a member who never writes a story still
       has their pictures.
sections.testing_checklist:
Stories
    ☐ A story cannot be created for a trip that is still open.
    ☐ A second story for the same trip is refused.
    ☐ Deactivating a prompt removes it from new stories and leaves existing answers displayed.
    ☐ A member cannot open another member’s story.
    ☐ Answers survive a closed browser without an explicit save.
